title: Failure Surface Explorer — tracehook stitching, adaptive sampling, and unified error lanes
creator: Aria Patel
description: Build a Failure Surface Explorer: a correlated observability experience that surfaces timeouts, overload conditions, model-level errors, and HTTP/gRPC response codes across routing, batching, and KV cache boundaries. Goal is to help oncall and SREs rapidly identify whether an error spike is caused by client retries, upstream throttling, runtime overload, model rejections, or network/transcoding failures. This ticket covers tracehook stitching, enrichment of metrics/log pipelines, adaptive trace sampling, and a new dashboard surface that prioritizes failure lanes by SLO exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Tracehook middleware is deployed to inference gateways and attaches: route_id, model_id, model_version, batch_id, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, kernel_variant to all spans
Adaptive sampling reduces trace volume by 75% on normal traffic while preserving >=95% coverage of error spike windows
Metrics pipeline emits enriched error counters and latency histograms (p50/p90/p99) partitioned by route/model/version and failure_category
Failure Surface Explorer dashboard shows per-route heatmap of failure lanes, stacked SLO exposure, and example traces for top 3 contributing failure categories
Runbook links and automated escalation actions appear in the dashboard for high-impact lanes (timeout, overload, model-rejection)

End-to-end test: simulate 5 failure modes (client timeout, request surge/backpressure, model OOM, invalid input rejection, HTTP 502 upstream) and verify dashboard attribution matches simulated root cause
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff with SRE, Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed schema for trace enrichment fields and initial failure_category enum: TIMEOUT, OVERLOAD, MODEL_ERROR, CLIENT_ERR, NETWORK, UPSTREAM

2026-03-01: Prototype tracehook implemented as OpenTelemetry middleware. Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prs/1289 — attaches model metadata and batch context. TODO: make batch_id stable across retries

2026-03-04: Design sync with Console team to wire example traces into new dashboard panel. Decision: use pre-aggregated OLAP tables for heatmaps (ClickHouse) and keep raw spans in trace store for drilldown
2026-03-07: Performance tradeoff review: enrichment increases trace payload by ~12%. Ops comfortable given adaptive sampling and gzip. Action: add field-level sampling for large kernel_variant blob

2026-03-10: Implemented adaptive sampling controller prototype that increases sampling to 100% when error counter rate exceeds dynamic threshold. Unit tests added. Link to draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Failure+Surface+Explorer
2026-03-12: UX walkthrough with SRE and PM. Feedback: add explicit model-rejection subtypes (e.g., safety_reject, token_limit, oom). Added follow-up sub-issue for full model error taxonomy mapping
technical_notes: Tracehook stitching approach: inject synthetic parent span at gateway that records routing and batching decisions, then attach child spans from runtime. Use trace id to join run-level metadata with per-model spans.

Failure attribution heuristic: prefer runtime-detected signals (batch_backpressure, kv_lock_timeout, model_rejection_code) before inferring from HTTP codes. HTTP/gRPC codes will be fall-through signal.
Adaptive sampling: two-stage controller — baseline probabilistic sampling (0.1%) + error-aware burst sampler that ramps to 100% for traces with non-2xx responses or SLO-violating latency buckets
Storage plan: OLAP aggregated table (hourly) for heatmaps with dimensions [route, model_id, model_version, failure_category, latency_bucket], raw span retention kept at 14 days for drilldown
Security: PII in inputs must be redacted before spans leave customer-controlled Private deployments. For hosted, use KMS-backed token masking. See security note in Confluence page.
Compatibility: ensure tracehook labels are present for both HTTP and gRPC stack (gateway + direct runtime clients) and for Dedicated customers the labels are emitted but flagged as optional
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: trace payload growth and higher egress costs. Mitigation: field-level sampling, gzip, and OLAP aggregation to reduce retention of full spans.
Risk: misattribution when multiple failure signals present (e.g., overload + model rejection). Mitigation: apply prioritized scoring and surface top-2 causes with confidence scores in dashboard.
Risk: noisy alerts from increased sampling during incidents. Mitigation: route alerts through SLO burn rate AND absolute error thresholds before paging oncall
